source_refs.note: Exercise 5.2, Question 2 (book p. 158); answer key PDF 306

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find the angle from the line with slope \(m_1\) to the line with slope \(m_2\), where \(m_1 = 2\), \(m_2 = -\frac{1}{2}\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein slopes seedhe diye hue hain, points se nikalne ki zaroorat nahi.
Lekin formula lagane se pehle ek cheez dekhni hai: \(1 + m_1 m_2\). Agar yeh zero ho to formula mein zero se divide hoga, aur iska matlab hai lines perpendicular hain.
Plan: \(m_1 m_2\) check karein, phir angle batayein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(m_1 = 2\), \(m_2 = -\frac{1}{2}\).
Maloom karna: pehli line se doosri line tak angle \(\theta\).
Tareeqa: Theorem 7 ke liye \(1 + m_1 m_2 \ne 0\) zaroori hai; Corollary 2 kehta hai ke \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\) ho to lines perpendicular hain.

\(1 + m_1 m_2\) nikalein
\[m_1 m_2 = 2 \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -1\]
\[1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\]
Kyun: Theorem 7 ka denominator zero ho gaya, is liye \(\tan\theta\) ki koi value nahi (undefined).
Dhyan dein: yahan formula mein zabardasti values rakh kar 'infinity' likhne ki bajaye seedha Corollary 2 lagayein.
Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: ek slope ko ulta kar ke us ka sign badal dein to perpendicular line ka slope milta hai; 2 ka ulta \(\frac{1}{2}\), sign badla to \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

Natija
\[\theta = 90^\circ\]
Kyun: Corollary 2: \(\ell_1 \perp \ell_2\) agar aur sirf agar \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 0\).

Tasdeeq:
Slopes \(2\) aur \(-\frac{1}{2}\) ek doosre ke negative reciprocal hain (ulta kar ke sign badla), jo perpendicular lines ki pehchaan hai \(\checkmark\)
Khulasa: jab bhi \(m_1 m_2 = -1\) nazar aaye, seedha \(90^\circ\) likh dein; formula chalane ki zaroorat hi nahi.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Find the angle from the line with slope \(m_1\) to the line with slope \(m_2\), where \(m_1 = 3\), \(m_2 = -2\).
blocks.explanation:
Slopes diye hue hain, aur \(1 + m_1 m_2 = 1 - 6 = -5 \ne 0\), is liye Theorem 7 seedha lagta hai.
Order yaad rakhein: 'from' slope \(m_1 = 3\), 'to' slope \(m_2 = -2\).
Plan: values rakhein, simplify karein, angle parhein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(m_1 = 3\), \(m_2 = -2\).
Maloom karna: pehli line se doosri line tak angle \(\theta\).
Tareeqa: Theorem 7, \(\tan\theta = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1 m_2}\).

Theorem 7 lagayein
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{-2 - 3}{1 + (3)(-2)}\]
\[= \dfrac{-5}{-5} = 1\]
Kyun: numerator mein pehle \(m_2 = -2\). Upar neeche dono negative, is liye jawab positive.
Dhyan dein: \(-2 - 3 = -5\) hai, \(-1\) nahi; signs dhyan se.

Angle parhein
\[\theta = \tan^{-1} 1 = 45^\circ\]
Kyun: \(\tan 45^\circ = 1\), aur positive tan ka matlab acute angle.

Tasdeeq:
\[\tan 45^\circ = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Agar order ulta karte to \(\tan\theta = -1\) aata, yani \(135^\circ = 180^\circ - 45^\circ\); yeh bhi samajh mein aata hai kyunke ulta ghoomne se doosra supplementary angle milta hai.
Khulasa: 'from' aur 'to' ki tarteeb hi tay karti hai ke jawab \(45^\circ\) hai ya \(135^\circ\); is sawal mein \(m_1 = 3\) se \(m_2 = -2\) tak ghoomna tha, is liye \(45^\circ\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein ek part '(iii) \(120^\circ\)' bhi chhapa hai, jab ke Question 2 ke sirf do parts (i) aur (ii) hain. Is liye yeh line kisi chhape hue part ki nahi. (i) ka \(90^\circ\) aur (ii) ka \(45^\circ\) bilkul sahi hain.
